title: Piano Quintet in E-flat major
hook: Written for Clara in a few weeks, the work that made piano and string quartet a team.

painting.title: A Symphony
painting.pairingNote: Piano, strings and voices making music together in a Romantic drawing room: the world of music at home that Schumann’s quintet brought into the concert hall.

facts: Schumann wrote the quintet in a few weeks in September and October 1842, in what is called his “year of chamber music”. Until then he had written almost nothing but piano music and songs; that year brought three string quartets, this quintet and a piano quartet.

He dedicated it to his wife Clara, the great pianist. She was to play it at its first private performance in December 1842, but fell ill, and Felix Mendelssohn sight-read the difficult piano part instead. His suggestions led Schumann to revise the inner movements, adding a second [[trio|trio]] to the scherzo.
Clara played it at the first public performance, at the Leipzig Gewandhaus on 8 January 1843, and called it “splendid, full of vigour and freshness”. She performed it often for the rest of her life.

Its success made piano and string quartet a favourite combination: Brahms, Dvořák and many others followed. The piano sometimes converses with the strings and sometimes faces them like a soloist with an orchestra.
bigPicture.inOneLine: an exuberant opening (I), a funeral march with a storm inside (II), a scherzo of rushing scales (III), a finale that ends by combining its own theme with the first movement’s (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro brillante
movements.summary: All five players launch a bold theme of huge upward leaps. Then the music melts into one of Schumann’s most tender melodies, a duet for cello and viola. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]; in its middle the piano races in quick figures while the strings hammer out the opening theme.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, all five
mainIdeas.description: a confident tune in long notes that leaps upwards in wide steps.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, cello and viola
mainIdeas.description: a soft, yearning melody, passed from one to the other.

notice: Listen for the cello and viola in the second theme. Schumann gives the most tender music of the movement not to the violins or the piano but to the two lower strings.
In the development, notice how the piano becomes a soloist, racing around while the four strings play together like a small orchestra.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Andsnes and the Artemis Quartet recorded the quintet at the Teldex Studio in Berlin in December 2006. They play the repeat of the exposition. On the Spotify album the quintet is tracks 1–4, followed by Brahms’s Piano Quintet.

movements.heading: In modo d'una marcia. Un poco largamente
movements.tempo: In modo d'una marcia. Un poco largamente
movements.summary: A funeral march in C minor, quiet and halting, with a melody in the first violin over the piano’s dragging steps. It alternates with a warm, singing song and, at the centre, a wild, agitated storm in the piano. The march keeps coming back, each time a little changed. Ingmar Bergman used it as the main theme of his film *Fanny and Alexander* (1982).

mainIdeas.name: The march
mainIdeas.description: a sombre, halting tune in the first violin, over hushed, limping chords in the piano.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a long, sweet melody for violin and cello in C major.

mainIdeas.name: The storm
mainIdeas.description: fast, surging piano figures under urgent string chords; it is the march theme in disguise.

stops.hear: Very quiet: the first violin plays a sombre, halting melody; the piano answers with dragging chords
stops.happening: The funeral march, in C minor

stops.hear: A warm, singing melody for the first violin and cello, over flowing piano chords
stops.happening: The first episode, in C major

stops.hear: The march returns, still quiet
stops.happening: The march again

stops.hear: Suddenly fast and loud: the piano storms in rushing figures, the strings cut in with urgent chords
stops.happening: The *Agitato* episode, in F minor. The march theme is hidden inside it

stops.hear: The march returns, now over quick, restless notes in the piano, with new lines in the violin and cello
stops.happening: The march transformed by the storm

stops.hear: The singing melody returns in a new key, with a richer piano part
stops.happening: The first episode again, in F major

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The march one last time, fading away
stops.happening: A quiet close in C minor

notice: Listen to the piano in the first minute. It barely moves: short, heavy chords that sound like slow footsteps.
Compare the march before and after the storm. The second time, the piano no longer drags but ripples underneath, and the violin and cello add lines of their own.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Molto vivace
movements.summary: The [[scherzo|scherzo]] is built almost entirely on scales, rushing up and down. It has two trios: the first a gentle [[canon|canon]] between violin and viola, the second, added after Mendelssohn’s advice, a fierce, unbroken stream of quick notes.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo
mainIdeas.description: loud, bounding scales in a skipping rhythm, up and down the instruments.

mainIdeas.name: Trio I
mainIdeas.description: a soft, lyrical tune that the violin and viola play one after the other.

mainIdeas.name: Trio II
mainIdeas.description: a racing, heavily accented line in a different, two-beat metre.

notice: In Trio I, listen for the echo: the viola plays the violin’s tune a moment later, like a round.

movements.heading: Allegro ma non troppo
movements.summary: The finale starts in the wrong key, in G minor, with a stamping, minor-key theme, and stays away from the home key for a long time. Only near the middle does E-flat major arrive. Then, in the closing minutes, Schumann combines the finale’s theme with the first movement’s opening theme in a grand double [[fugato|fugato]].

mainIdeas.name: Theme A
mainIdeas.description: a stamping, determined tune in the minor.

mainIdeas.name: Theme B
mainIdeas.description: a brighter, bouncing idea in the major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme C
mainIdeas.description: a calm, lyrical melody in a distant key.

mainIdeas.name: The return
mainIdeas.description: the first movement’s opening theme, in long notes, combined with Theme A.

notice: Near the end, listen for the first movement’s leaping theme in long notes. When you recognise it, the whole quintet comes full circle.

threads.title: Piano and quartet
threads.body: Schumann alternates conversation among five equals with passages where the piano faces the four strings like a soloist facing an orchestra.

threads.title: Coming full circle
threads.body: The finale brings back the first movement’s theme, an example of [[cyclic-form|cyclic form]].

threads.title: Clara
threads.body: The quintet was written for and dedicated to Clara Schumann, and she kept it in her concerts for decades.
